rationale: Recurring throughout this page (lines 12, 15, 19, 27) as creatures-with-teeth-and-tusks who stand on feet before the cosmic being. Etymology unclear: possibly related to ⲱⲱⲙⲉ 'jaw, swallow' (his biters/devourers), or to a Lycopolitan plural noun for subordinate-forces. Translated 'beasts' on the basis of the dental armament (line 19) and bestial behavior.
Lines 14, 17 in parallel with ⲛⲉϩⲟ̄ⲁⲙ. Likely Greek-derived — either μυριάδες 'myriads' or μέρη 'members.' 'Myriads' fits the relational context (he addresses, hides from, reveals himself to them).
Line 16, paired with ⲟⲩⲍⲱⲧⲃⲉ 'a killing' as a violence-doublet. Possibly cognate with ϣⲱⲱⲣ/ϣⲱⲣϣⲣ 'destruction.' Tentative.
Line 24, paired with ⲥⲉⲧⲉ 'fire' as a phenomenon of the body. Possibly related to native ⲙⲡⲉ 'thunder' or ⲉⲃⲣⲏϭⲉ 'lightning.' Tentative.

Line 23 (after 'demons and'), apparently a Lycopolitan abbreviated form of γίγαντες 'giants' — the standard second member of the demons-and-giants Manichaean pair as offspring of Hyle. Confidence moderate.
Line 34: 'in his ⲍⲡ̄ⲧⲉ.' Lyc. for ϩⲏⲡⲧⲉ/ϩⲏⲡⲉ 'belly.' Continues the body-mapping after face.
Line 19: ⲛⲁⲃⲍⲉ ⲙⲛ̄ ⲛ̄ⲓ̈ⲉⲃⲉ 'teeth and tusks.' Lyc. ⲛⲁⲃⲍⲉ = Sah. ⲛⲁϫϩⲉ 'teeth' (with regular Lyc. ⲍ for ϫ).
Line 19: paired with ⲛⲁⲃⲍⲉ 'teeth.' Lyc. for ⲉⲓⲃϩⲉ 'molar/fang' or related dental term.
Line 31: ⲛ̄ⲥⲉⲧⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲁⲩ ⲁⲣⲁϩ 'they yield themselves to him.' From ⲧⲟⲩⲟ 'show, declare, hand-over' with reflexive sense. Contrasts with the preceding ⲁⲛⲁⲭⲱⲣⲉ 'withdraw.'
Lines 28, 30, 31. Lyc. compound preposition ϩⲓⲑⲏ 'before, in front' with possessive ⲉϩ-ⲍⲏ. Spatial 'before his face/before him.'

Line 21: ⲛⲧⲁⲩⲙⲁⲁⲛⲕϥ̄ 'they fashioned him.' From the verb ⲙⲁⲛⲕ̄ 'mold, shape' — synonymous with πλάσσειν that follows. The double-fashioning verb (ⲙⲁⲛⲕ̄ + ⲡⲡⲗⲁⲥⲥⲉ) emphasizes the molded nature of his impenetrable body.
